text:
Maria G.: Heads-up — got a pile of customer tickets about tail latency after the 2026-03 model rollout. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms, p99 to ~2.4s for a subset of requests. Some customers are seeing retries.
AJ: I noticed the same on traces — spikes correlate with certain long-prefix chat sessions. GPU mem usage creeping up and fragmentation looks likely.
Tyler H.: Logs from the runtime show repeated CUDA alloc failures followed by slow fallbacks to CPU path which explains the big p99. nvml shows resident memory steady but free blocks fragmented.
Iris (oncall): Alert page: https://internal/alerts/206789 — alerts for OOM/alloc-fail and high latency. I've throttled one high-volume org to reduce pressure.
Devon S.: Could be KV cache growth — we rolled larger kv_cache for the rollout to improve reuse with long contexts. If kv never shrinks with rare evictions -> fragmentation.
AJ: Repro steps I used locally: run loadgen with 350 concurrent clients + long prefix (~8k tokens) to the canary model. Command: ```python loadgen.py --model redwood-v2-canary --concurrency 350 --prefix-size 8000``` and watch p99.
Tyler H.: Collected a couple dumps: /var/log/runtime/gpu-mem-dump-206789-*.tgz uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/gpu-frag/ — nvprof and nvml snippets show many small free blocks.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2067890123, severity: high, owners: @Iris (oncall), @Devon S.
Maria G.: Immediate mitigations I tried: 1) route traffic from canary -> stable for noisy tenants (cut p99 by ~40%); 2) disable kv_cache for affected model variant (drops reuse but reduces memory growth); 3) scheduled rolling restart of 3 GPUS on the pool to defrag.
Iris (oncall): After routing and restarting two nodes p95 recovered to ~220ms, p99 ~1.1s. Still some pods show slow allocation spikes.
Devon S.: Long-term options: 1) add eviction for kv_cache based on working set size; 2) tune allocator to coalesce free blocks (we have a patch that enables periodic compaction in our allocator branch); 3) cap per-request KV growth and enforce max_kv_bytes.
AJ: Quick patch I can try: enable jemalloc for the runtime process and toggle our allocator compaction at runtime via /admin/allocator?compact=1. Doing that now on a non-prod pool.
Tyler H.: Note: calling torch.cuda.empty_cache() in the worker loop won't fix fragmentation caused by many small allocations; it only returns to driver. Real fix is coalescing or restart.
Maria G.: Customer-facing note drafted for CS: "We're investigating a latency regression tied to GPU memory fragmentation after a model rollout. Temporary mitigations include routing to stable model, scheduled restarts, and disabling KV cache for affected tenants. We'll update in 2h or when we have root cause."
Iris (oncall): Action list: 1) AJ to try allocator compaction on staging (ETA 1h). 2) Devon to add short-term kv_cache LRU/ejection rule (ETA 3h). 3) Tyler to run targeted load repro and attach perf traces (ETA 2h). 4) Maria to coordinate CS comms and keep customers throttled as needed.
Devon S.: Also adding a metric to track per-pod fragmented_free_ratio and kv_cache_bytes_per_shard so we can alert earlier.
AJ: Running compaction test now. If it works I'll promote to the affected nodes and post results here.
Maria G.: Thanks — please paste commands, outputs, and the exact node IDs you restart. We're keeping this thread as the single source of truth for the support tickets linked in the incident.
Iris (oncall): updating incident and pinging sales for any escalated accounts.
Maria G.: FYI, nobody should rollback the model yet — we need telemetry from compaction tests to confirm root cause, but rollback is on table if mitigations don't hold.
AJ: Update: compaction on staging reduced peak alloc latency from ~400ms to ~70ms for my load test. Will run it on 3 affected nodes in 15m.
Tyler H.: I'll capture metrics during that window and compare token service times.
Maria G.: Great. Keep notes of exact commands and file uploads to S3 for postmortem.
